idiom.title: Fight an uphill battle
idiom.glossZh: “艰难地奋斗” 或 “面临艰巨的挑战”。
idiom.interpretationEn: This phrase originates from a military term, referring to soldiers having a harder time fighting uphill due to their disadvantageous position. Over time, the phrase has been adopted into everyday language to describe any difficult task or challenge that requires significant effort to overcome.
idiom.interpretationZh: 这个短语源于军事术语，指士兵们在上坡时作战会更艰难，因地势较低的一方处于劣势。后来，这个短语被借用到日常生活中，用来形容一件很困難并需要付出极大努力去争取成功的事。

examples.en: Starting a new business in this economy feels like fighting an uphill battle.
examples.zh: 在当前的经济环境下创业感觉就像在艰难地奋斗。

examples.en: He knew he was fighting an uphill battle trying to change the company’s old habits.
examples.zh: 他知道试图改变公司的陈旧习惯是一场艰难地奋斗。

examples.en: She’s been fighting an uphill battle to gain recognition in her field.
examples.zh: 她一直在艰难地奋斗，试图在她的领域获得认可。

people.name: Joshua Ferris
people.extract: Joshua Ferris is an American author best known for his debut novel Then We Came to the End (2007). The novel is a comedy about the American workplace, is narrated in the first-person plural, and is set in a fictitious Chicago ad agency facing challenges at the end of the 1990s Internet boom.
highlights: Author of debut novel Then We Came to the End (2007).
Novel is a comedy about the American workplace.

people.name: Michael D. Brown
people.bio: Director of the U.S. Federal Emergency Management Agency from 2003 to 2005
people.extract: Michael DeWayne Brown is an American attorney, and former government official who served as the administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) from 2003 to 2005. He joined FEMA as general counsel in 2001 and became deputy director the same year. Appointed in January 2003 by President George W. Bush to lead FEMA, Brown resigned in September 2005 following his controversial handling of Hurricane Katrina. Brown currently hosts a radio talk show on 630 KHOW in Denver, Colorado.
highlights: Joined FEMA as general counsel in 2001.
Resigned from FEMA after Hurricane Katrina.
